elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) expressly requires TrueLink to defend Client against third-party claims alleging that the Interface, Hosting Services, or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) expressly requires TrueLink to indemnify Client against the specified third-party IP claims.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer's affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) protects only Client. Although Section 12(b) names affiliates, it does not provide a defense obligation or an express IP-infringement trigger.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer's affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The IP indemnity in Section 12(c) is limited to Client and does not identify Client's affiliates as indemnitees.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: There is no defense obligation triggered by TrueLink's breach of law. Section 12(b) addresses contractual breach or failure to perform, not an independent breach-of-law trigger.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: No express indemnity trigger covers TrueLink's breach of law; coverage under Section 12(b) would exist only if the conduct also constituted a breach of the Agreement.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no Vendor-caused data-breach trigger or corresponding defense obligation.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no express indemnity for a data breach caused by TrueLink.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is not an express indemnity trigger, and no defense duty applies to such claims.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 12(b) nor Section 12(c) expressly covers claims arising from TrueLink's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is not an express trigger, and no corresponding defense obligation is stated.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 12(b) nor Section 12(c) expressly covers claims arising from TrueLink's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require the indemnitee to provide notice of a covered claim.
elements.evidence: No notice procedure appears in Section 12.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must address the indemnifying party's control of the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) imposes a defense duty but contains no language governing control of the defense or settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require reasonable cooperation from the indemnitee.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears in Section 12.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a)(iii) covers claims arising out of or relating to Client Content, including content posted by Client or its personnel.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a)(ii) covers claims resulting from a Client act or omission constituting a violation of state or federal law, rule, or regulation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 12(a) is materially broader: it also covers any breach of the Agreement, specified System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement consequences, the Web Site generally, conduct of Client customers, and injury or property damage from products, services, or information transmitted from the Web Site.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) expressly applies to 'any third-party claim.'

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must cover claims alleging that Vendor-provided services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) covers claims alleging that the Interface, Hosting Services, or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered IP claims.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) states that TrueLink 'shall defend' Client.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered IP claims.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) states that TrueLink 'shall ... indemnify' Client.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims arising from Customer's modifications.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) excludes claims arising from Client's modifications.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims arising from Customer's combinations with other products or services.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) excludes claims arising from Client's combination of the covered items with other products or services.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity may exclude claims arising from Customer's specifications.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) excludes claims arising from Client's specifications.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) permits TrueLink to procure for Client the right to continue using the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to modify the affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) permits TrueLink to modify the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor must have a remedy to replace the affected item.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) permits TrueLink to replace the affected item.

elements.element: Vendor must refund fees for the affected item if procurement, modification, and replacement are unavailable.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) requires a refund of fees paid for the affected item if none of the preceding remedies is available.

elements.element: Vendor's liability for the IP indemnity must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 12(c) caps TrueLink's total liability under that subsection at 3x the annual fees paid by Client under the Agreement.

result.reason: The added Section 12(c) supplies the complete fallback IP indemnity, including defense and indemnification, the three stated exclusions, the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy sequence, and a 3x annual-fees cap. It does not achieve the preferred position because affiliates are omitted from the IP indemnity, the Vendor law-breach, Vendor-caused data-breach, gross-negligence, and wilful-misconduct triggers are absent, no indemnification procedures are included, and Client's indemnity remains substantially broader than content and breach of law. The change is otherwise targeted and leaves the existing indemnities operative. Drafting quality is reduced because 'annual fees paid' lacks a measurement period and the relationship between overlapping Section 12(b) claims and the Section 12(c)-only cap is not clarified.
